subject: Cloud Computing
title: Physical Security Measures
description: A 60-second lesson on Physical Security Measures.

hook.text: You can't just walk into a cloud data center. Most are designed to look like anonymous warehouses.

buildup.text: Fences, guards, mantraps, biometric scanners, and security cameras protect every entrance.

discovery.text: Inside, access is zone-based. Most employees can only reach the areas their badge allows.

twist.text: When hard drives are retired, they're physically shredded — not just wiped — to prevent data theft.

climax.text: Cloud providers invest more in physical security than most banks. Your data may be safer there.

punchline.text: The cloud is guarded like a fortress. A very boring fortress.

quiz.question: What happens to hard drives when they are retired from cloud data centers?
options: They are physically shredded to prevent any data recovery
They are donated to schools and charities
They are reformatted and sold to consumers

details.summary: Cloud data centers employ multi-layered physical security including perimeter fencing, security guards, biometric access controls, mantrap entrances, 24/7 surveillance, and strict visitor policies. Physical access is restricted to authorized personnel on a need-to-enter basis.
details.whyItMatters: Physical security prevents unauthorized access to hardware that stores millions of customers' data. Compromising a physical server could bypass all software security measures.
takeaways: Multi-layer security includes fences, guards, and biometrics
Mantrap entrances prevent tailgating into secure areas
Even employees need specific authorization for each area

faq.question: Can anyone visit a cloud data center?
faq.answer: Cloud providers rarely allow visitors inside active data centers. AWS, Google, and Azure all restrict physical access to essential personnel only. Even authorized employees cannot access areas outside their specific work zone. Visitors require executive approval and constant escort.

faq.question: How is hardware decommissioned securely?
faq.answer: When hardware reaches end of life, drives are cryptographically erased, degaussed, and physically shredded. Chain of custody is documented throughout the destruction process. This ensures that customer data cannot be recovered from decommissioned equipment.
